args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy - rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the v2.3.1 production deploy (error rate was 0.18). I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production, in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). Post-rollback status: v2.3.0 in all three regions, healthy=true, error rate 0.002. v2.3.1 is marked unhealthy in production. Not yet investigated: root cause of the v2.3.1 failure. Follow-up: investigate v2.3.1 before redeploying it. Note that v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and opened a SEV2 incident.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.1 was the latest release and was unhealthy in production. v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to it. The rollback completed. Status now shows v2.3.0 in every region, healthy, with an error rate of 0.002, down from 0.18 on v2.3.1.
- **Incident:** Opened as SEV2 for checkout-api, and it paged the on-call engineer. The summary describes the rollback and the post-rollback status. It also notes that the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure is not yet investigated, and that v2.3.1-rc was unhealthy in staging.

v2.3.1 should not be redeployed until someone has investigated it. Redeploying it would also need change-manager approval, since it has never been healthy in production.

content.text: The latest production release is v2.3.1, which is unhealthy. The most recent production release that was healthy is v2.3.0, so I'll roll back to that.
